text:
Sam (Sales): FYI customer POC hit a 413 when sending their full conversation + attachments. They say ~18k tokens in context, ~8MB JSON payload. Error: `413 Payload Too Large` from our gateway. Need quick workaround for tomorrow demo.
Alex: Ouch. Gateway/nginx default body_limit is probably 8M. Do we have a hard cap in the API proxy?
Maria: We have a 10MB limit enforced at the ingress layer for hosted customers currently. That explains it. The model itself can handle 32k tokens, but the transport is choking. :grimacing:
Sam (Sales): Customer expects native long-context support — demo tomorrow. Can we do anything fast or do we need a change?
Jon: Short-term options: 1) gzip the request body (we accept compressed payloads) 2) send the large context as an S3 presigned URL (we fetch server-side) 3) chunk the context into multiple requests and stitch client-side.
Emily: For demo I'd recommend presigned URL -> we fetch and stream into the model, avoids hitting proxy body limits. It's also good for attachments.
Alex: Confirming we support server-side fetch of a customer-hosted URL if they include `context_url` in the request. But that path is behind a feature flag for hosted tenants — not enabled for this account yet.
Sam (Sales): Can we flip the flag for this tenant temporarily? They signed an MSA but account provisioning hasn't completed.
Maria: Ops: flipping that flag requires a data-plane config change + audit log. I can do it but need approval and an explicit support ticket. Also note AWS S3 presigned URLs are best (no auth required).
Sam (Sales): I'll open the ticket now and tell them to generate a presigned S3 put/get link.
Emily: Meanwhile, quick workaround suggestions for their engineers: 1) client-side summarization of older context 2) store long docs in embeddings + retrieval (reduce tokens) 3) use chunked streaming to send only the most relevant window.
Alex: If they want an engineering fix: we could temporarily raise ingress body limit to 50MB for that tenant's gateway instance, but that's risky for noisy traffic and needs infra signoff.
Jon: Agree. Raising globally is a NO. Per-tenant routing change possible if they use a dedicated gateway (not enabled for this account). So presigned URL is lowest risk.
Sam (Sales): Ticket created: ENG-POC-4521. I've attached their example payload (sanitized). They can produce presigned GET for the `conversation.json` and we fetch. Customer is ok to try presigned GET.
deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-20T22:04:12Z: feature-flag-service updated for tenant toggles (no change applied).
Maria: I toggled the feature flag in the sandbox tenant for testing only. Can someone confirm the fetch path works with their sample presigned URL?
Emily: I tested locally with a public S3 presigned GET — our fetch code streams into the model and respects tokenization, worked fine with a ~12MB file.
Sam (Sales): Customer provided presigned URL and the demo on their side now hits our fetch path successfully. No 413. Demo scheduled for 10:00 PT tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Alex: Follow-ups: - Add a validation error message that suggests using presigned URL / gzip when payload > 8MB - Add doc snippet + sample curl for presigned GET path - Track infra ticket to consider per-tenant gateway for enterprise deals.
Sam (Sales): Perfect. I'll update the customer and include the curl sample. Thanks all for the quick turnaround.
Maria: Filing docs PR with examples and a short note about base64 overhead (embedding attachments as base64 increases payload size ~33%).
Sam (Sales): One last ask — can we add a short note in pricing guide about large-context costs? Customer asked if streaming/fetch affects billing.
Emily: It should be the same token billing; we'll add a line to the FAQ.
Sam (Sales): Awesome. Closing this thread unless anything else pops up.
